items.title: Compact isotopic submanifolds have isomorphic normal bundles and diffeomorphic complements
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $N$ be a smooth manifold without boundary, let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold and let $f_0,f_1:M	o N$ be isotopic embeddings with normal bundles $
u_0=f_0^*TN/TM$ and $
u_1=f_1^*TN/TM$ ([[def-normal-and-conormal-bundles-of-an-embedded-submanifold]]). Then $
u_0\cong
u_1$ as smooth vector bundles over $M$ and $N\setminus f_0(M)\cong N\setminus f_1(M)$; under AC every characteristic class defined on these normal bundles agrees (for orientation-dependent classes, use orientations transported by the displayed bundle isomorphism) and the complements are diffeomorphic. The example verifies the two embedding invariants supplied by isotopy: the ambient diffeomorphism of [[cor-isotopic-embeddings-have-diffeomorphic-complements]] intertwines the normal bundles, and [[thm-isotopy-extension]] is the source of that diffeomorphism. (The converse fails: trivial normal bundles do not force isotopy, as the reflected-sphere counterexample on this page shows.)
items.strategy: Let $H$ be the ambient isotopy of [[thm-isotopy-extension]] with $H_t\circ f_0=F_t$ and $H\circ f_0=f_1$. Its differential restricts to a bundle isomorphism $TN|_{f_0(M)}\to TN|_{f_1(M)}$ covering $f_1\circ f_0^{-1}$; on the level of $M$ it induces a bundle map $\nu_0\to\nu_1$ over the identity of $M$ because the tangent summand $TM$ is carried to $TM$ by the chain rule $dH\circ df_0=df_1$. A bundle map that is an isomorphism on each fibre is a bundle isomorphism, so characteristic classes agree. The complement statement is [[cor-isotopic-embeddings-have-diffeomorphic-complements]]. The parenthetical failure of the converse is the content of the reflected-sphere counterexample on this page. Countable choice is inherited.

items.strategy: Clause 1: both maps are immersions, and [[thm-smale-classification-of-sphere-immersions-in-euclidean-space]], clause 3, records that for $m=2,n=3$ all immersions $S^2\to\mathbb R^3$ are regularly homotopic because $\pi_2(SO(3))=0$; the formal-data computation is the one of the DT-26 pair, consumed here through its classification theorem ([[cor-regular-homotopy-classes-of-immersions-are-formal-homotopy-classes]]). Note that the contradiction is obtained through the isotopy extension theorem of this page, so the example also exercises [[thm-isotopy-extension]]. items.title: The double point dimension count for surfaces in four- and five-space
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M^2$ be a closed connected surface ($m=2$). Then:

1. for a self-transverse immersion $f:M^2\looparrowright\mathbb R^4$ the expected dimension is $2m-n=0$: the double point locus is a closed $0$-dimensional submanifold of $M\times M\setminus\Delta_M$, the double point set is finite, and the selected branch pairs are isolated and transverse; several pairs may initially have the same collision image;
2. for a self-transverse immersion $f:M^2\looparrowright\mathbb R^5$ the expected dimension is $-1<0$: the double point locus is empty, so $f$ is an injective immersion, and since $M$ is closed $f$ is an embedding.

The example shows why dimension four is the critical case for surfaces: it is exactly there that the double points are isolated rather than absent, so that the algebraic branch-pair count can be nonzero; the $m\ge3$ disjunction theorem does not cover this surface-in-four-space case. In five-space the configuration space argument already forbids double points.
items.strategy: Both clauses are the dimension count [[lem-double-point-locus-has-expected-dimension-two-m-minus-n]] specialised to $m=2$: the locus is a closed embedded submanifold of dimension $2m-n$ when that is nonnegative, and empty when it is negative. For clause 1, local injectivity of the immersion ([[cor-every-immersion-is-locally-an-embedding]]) together with compactness of $M$ gives a neighbourhood of the diagonal in $M\times M$ containing no double point pair, so $\Delta_2(f)$ is a closed subset of the compact complement of that neighbourhood; being 0-dimensional it is discrete and compact, hence finite, and so is its image $\Sigma(f)$. For clause 2, emptiness of the double point locus is injectivity ([[def-self-transverse-immersion-and-double-point-locus]]), and an injective immersion from closed $M$ is an embedding by the proper injective immersion criterion ([[prop-a-proper-injective-immersion-is-a-smooth-embedding]]). Countable choice is inherited from the transversality items.
